content: Ceftriaxone for injection can be administered intravenously. It is critical to avoid using diluents containing calcium, such as Ringer’s solution or Hartmann’s solution, for reconstituting ceftriaxone vials or for further diluting a reconstituted vial for IV administration, as this can lead to the formation of precipitates. Precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium can also occur when ceftriaxone is mixed with calcium-containing solutions in the same IV administration line. Ceftriaxone must not be administered simultaneously with calcium-containing IV solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions like parenteral nutrition via a Y-site. However, in patients other than neonates, ceftriaxone and calcium-containing solutions may be administered sequentially if the infusion lines are thoroughly flushed with a compatible fluid between infusions. There have been no reported interactions between ceftriaxone and oral calcium-containing products or between intramuscular ceftriaxone and calcium-containing products (IV or oral). In neonates, particularly those who are hyperbilirubinemic or premature, ceftriaxone is contraindicated. This is due to the risk of precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium if they require or are expected to require treatment with calcium-containing IV solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions such as parenteral nutrition. For pediatric patients, the recommended total daily dose for treating skin and skin structure infections is 50 to 75 mg/kg, administered once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. The total daily dose should not exceed 2 grams. For serious infections other than meningitis, the recommended total daily dose is also 50 to 75 mg/kg, given in divided doses every 12 hours, with a maximum daily dose of 2 grams. In the treatment of meningitis, an initial therapeutic dose of 100 mg/kg (not exceeding 4 grams) is recommended, followed by a total daily dose of 100 mg/kg/day (not exceeding 4 grams daily). This dose may be administered once daily or in equally divided doses every 12 hours, with the usual duration of therapy being 7 to 14 days. For adults, the usual daily dose is 1 to 2 grams, administered once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily, depending on the type and severity of the infection. For infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), a daily dose of 2 to 4 grams is recommended to achieve >90% target attainment, with a maximum daily dose of 4 grams. If Chlamydia trachomatis is a suspected pathogen, additional antichlamydial coverage should be included, as ceftriaxone has no activity against this organism. For preoperative use (surgical prophylaxis), a single dose of 1 gram administered intravenously 30 minutes to 2 hours before surgery is recommended. Ceftriaxone therapy should generally continue for at least 2 days after the signs and symptoms of infection have resolved. The usual duration of therapy is 4 to 14 days, but longer therapy may be required for complicated infections. For infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, therapy should be continued for at least 10 days. No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with renal or hepatic impairment. For proper use of the pharmacy bulk package, the 10-gram vial should be reconstituted with 95 mL of an appropriate IV diluent in a suitable work area, such as a laminar flow hood. The resulting solution will contain approximately 100 mg/mL of ceftriaxone. The vial closure may only be penetrated once using a sterile transfer device or dispensing set that allows measured distribution of the contents. Use of this product is restricted to a suitable work area, and withdrawal of container contents should be completed without delay. If this is not possible, a maximum of 4 hours from initial closure entry is permitted to complete fluid transfer operations. If reconstitution is necessary, this time limit begins with the introduction of solvent or diluent into the bulk package. Unused portions of the solution held longer than the recommended time periods should be discarded. Individual doses should be transferred to appropriate intravenous solutions as soon as possible following reconstitution of the bulk package. The stability of the solution after transfer into a container depends on the diluent, concentration, and temperature. Concentrations between 10 mg/mL and 40 mg/mL are recommended, although lower concentrations may be used if desired.
